Zymera · L2 navigation planners

What the planners do — and why the mission barely lets them

A demo of the four distilled path-planners, verified outside the simulator, then put back in its shoes.

Each agent's low-level controller is a learned path planner: give it a map and a goal, it floods a value field (bright near the goal) and the agent climbs it. Four architectures were distilled from a wavefront teacher — MVProp, GPPN, Highway-VIN, and a spatial-planning transformer (MSP). This page shows them planning on real maps they never trained on, then asks the honest question: how much of that ability survives the mission's partial observability.

3 · Verified outside the simulator

Nothing above uses our environment — just the planner net, an external map, and a BFS optimum. Across 256 real MovingAI maps plus independent generators (each planner run on maps drawn from a completely different process than ours), success at reaching the goal, and success within the planner's 32-step propagation range:

external sourceconv plannerMSPnaive Manhattanconv (within range, d≤16)
MovingAI · Dragon Age92%75%78%100%
MovingAI · maze73%48%49%99%
MovingAI · rooms36%19%21%80%
cellular caves95%91%84%100%
BSP rooms70%30%33%100%

BFS teacher = 100% everywhere (harness sanity). The conv planners beat naive on every source — real routing, and they generalize to unseen real maps within range. MSP sits at or below naive on structured maps: it did not learn to plan, only a distance heuristic that works in open space (caves). The overall dip on maze/room is long paths exceeding the 32-step range, not planning failure.

4 · The catch — the mission hides the map

That demo handed the planner the whole map. In the mission it never has it. Sensing radius is one cell, so almost all wall knowledge arrives by gossip over the comm graph; unknown cells are assumed open. Over an episode an agent's known-wall fraction climbs 0% → ~40% (mid) → ~74% (end), episode-mean ~40%, and near-blind early — exactly when the team is spreading out and routing would matter most.

5 · How much the planner is worth, by belief

% reach goal (all sources)empty (f=0)deploy (f≈0.4)f=0.8full (f=1.0)
conv planner47.751.759.465.1
MSP48.948.547.545.1
naive Manhattan (floor)46.946.946.946.9

At the belief the mission provides, the learned planner is ~5 points over a naive optimistic controller, and at an empty belief it is that controller (no walls known → the field is just distance → straight line). MSP never rises, and on real maps it degrades as walls are added — it mis-uses the information.

The honest read. The planners are competent — the full-map demo proves it, and they generalize to real maps outside our setup. But the mission keeps the map hidden, so their routing rarely engages: in deployment all four collapse toward optimistic goal-seeking, which is why the architecture choice barely moved the mission numbers. The leverage isn't the planner — it's getting the belief richer (more connectivity → more gossip → further right on these curves) and the higher-level coordination that decides where agents go.
